```plato
    //==
    // # Rigid pose operations
    //
    // Application, composition, inversion, interpolation, and matrix interchange for
    // the rigid poses of `transforms.types.plato`.

    //==
    // Rigid poses — position plus rotation; the natural "where is this object"
    // transform. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rigid_transformation

    // Apply the pose: rotate about the origin, then translate to Position.
    Transform(p: Point2D, pose: Pose2D): Point2D
        => pose.Position + p.PositionVector.Transform(pose.Rotation);

    // Alias for Transform with transform-on-left (* operator): pose * p.
    Multiply(pose: Pose2D, p: Point2D): Point2D
        => Transform(p, pose);

    // Rotate a displacement by the pose's rotation (translation does not act
    // on vectors).
    Transform(v: Vector2D, pose: Pose2D): Vector2D
        => v.Transform(pose.Rotation);

    // Alias for Transform with transform-on-left (* operator): pose * v.
    Multiply(pose: Pose2D, v: Vector2D): Vector2D
        => Transform(v, pose);

    // The pose that applies `first`, then `second`.
    Compose(first: Pose2D, second: Pose2D): Pose2D
        => (first.Position.Transform(second), first.Rotation * second.Rotation);

    // Alias for Compose, enabling the * operator: a * b applies a first.
    Multiply(a: Pose2D, b: Pose2D): Pose2D
        => a.Compose(b);

    // The pose that undoes this one: p' = R^-1 (p - t).
    Inverse(pose: Pose2D): Pose2D {
        var invRot = pose.Rotation.Inverse;
        return (pose.Position.PositionVector.Negative.Transform(invRot).ToPoint, invRot);
    }

    // Interpolate position and rotation independently; t is unclamped.
    Lerp(a: Pose2D, b: Pose2D, t: Number): Pose2D
        => (a.Position.Lerp(b.Position, t), a.Rotation.Lerp(b.Rotation, t));

    // The affine matrix of the pose (rotation, then translation).
    Matrix3x2(pose: Pose2D): Matrix3x2
        => pose.Rotation.Matrix3x2 * Matrix3x2.CreateTranslation(pose.Position.PositionVector);

    // The pose stored in a rigid affine matrix. Precondition: the matrix is a
    // rotation followed by a translation (no scale, shear, or reflection).
    Pose2D(m: Matrix3x2): Pose2D
        => (Point2D(m.Row3.X, m.Row3.Y), Rotation2D(m.Row1.Y.Atan2(m.Row1.X)));

    // Apply the pose: rotate about the origin, then translate to Position.
    Transform(p: Point3D, pose: Pose3D): Point3D
        => pose.Position + p.PositionVector.Transform(pose.Orientation);

    // Alias for Transform with transform-on-left (* operator): pose * p.
    Multiply(pose: Pose3D, p: Point3D): Point3D
        => Transform(p, pose);

    // Rotate a displacement by the pose's orientation.
    Transform(v: Vector3D, pose: Pose3D): Vector3D
        => v.Transform(pose.Orientation);

    // Alias for Transform with transform-on-left (* operator): pose * v.
    Multiply(pose: Pose3D, v: Vector3D): Vector3D
        => Transform(v, pose);

    // The pose that applies `first`, then `second`.
    Compose(first: Pose3D, second: Pose3D): Pose3D
        => (first.Position.Transform(second), first.Orientation.Concatenate(second.Orientation));

    // Alias for Compose, enabling the * operator: a * b applies a first.
    Multiply(a: Pose3D, b: Pose3D): Pose3D
        => a.Compose(b);

    // The pose that undoes this one: p' = R^-1 (p - t).
    Inverse(pose: Pose3D): Pose3D {
        var invQ = pose.Orientation.Inverse;
        return (pose.Position.PositionVector.Negative.Transform(invQ).ToPoint, invQ);
    }

    // Interpolate position linearly and orientation spherically; t is unclamped.
    Lerp(a: Pose3D, b: Pose3D, t: Number): Pose3D
        => (a.Position.Lerp(b.Position, t), a.Orientation.Slerp(b.Orientation, t));

    // The homogeneous matrix of the pose (rotation, then translation).
    Matrix4x4(pose: Pose3D): Matrix4x4
        => pose.Orientation.Matrix4x4 * Matrix4x4.CreateTranslation(pose.Position.PositionVector);

    // The pose stored in a rigid homogeneous matrix. Precondition: the matrix
    // is a rotation followed by a translation (no scale, shear, or projection).
    Pose3D(m: Matrix4x4): Pose3D
        => (m.Translation.ToPoint, m.Rotation);

    //==
    // Rigid conversions — the Pose obligations of `IRigid2D` / `IRigid3D`. Each
    // rigid representation names the pose it is: a translation is a pose with
    // the identity rotation, a rotation is a pose at the origin, a
    // rotation-about-a-centre is the conjugation of the two. Composition and
    // inversion of any two rigid transforms stay inside the family, which is
    // what the interface buys over IAffine2D/IAffine3D.

    // A translation is the pose at that offset with no rotation.
    Pose2D(t: Translation2D): Pose2D
        => (t.Vector.ToPoint, Rotation2D.Identity);

    // A translation is the pose at that offset with no rotation.
    Pose3D(t: Translation3D): Pose3D
        => (t.Vector.ToPoint, Quaternion.Identity);

    // A plane rotation is the pose at the origin with that rotation.
    Pose2D(r: Rotation2D): Pose2D
        => (Point2D.Origin, r);

    // A quaternion is the pose at the origin with that orientation.
    Pose3D(q: Quaternion): Pose3D
        => (Point3D.Origin, q);

    // Any 3D rotation representation is the pose at the origin with its
    // quaternion; this one body serves AxisAngle, EulerAngles and Rotor3D.
    Pose3D(r: IRotational3D): Pose3D
        => r.Quaternion.Pose3D;

    // Rotating about a centre: translate the centre to the origin, rotate,
    // translate back.
    Pose2D(r: RotationAbout2D): Pose2D {
        var c = r.Center.PositionVector;
        return ((c - c.Transform(r.Rotation)).ToPoint, r.Rotation);
    }

    // Rotating about a centre: translate the centre to the origin, rotate,
    // translate back.
    Pose3D(r: RotationAbout3D): Pose3D {
        var c = r.Center.PositionVector;
        return ((c - c.Transform(r.Rotation)).ToPoint, r.Rotation);
    }

    // Any rigid transform is affine, through the pose it names. Concrete
    // conversions on the individual types take precedence over this one.
    AffineTransform2D(x: IRigid2D): AffineTransform2D
        => x.Pose2D.AffineTransform2D;

    // Any rigid transform is affine, through the pose it names.
    AffineTransform3D(x: IRigid3D): AffineTransform3D
        => x.Pose3D.AffineTransform3D;

    // Rigid transforms are closed under composition: apply `first`, then
    // `second`, with no matrix round-trip and no drift out of the family.
    Compose(first: IRigid2D, second: IRigid2D): Pose2D
        => first.Pose2D.Compose(second.Pose2D);

    // Rigid transforms are closed under composition: apply `first`, then
    // `second`.
    Compose(first: IRigid3D, second: IRigid3D): Pose3D
        => first.Pose3D.Compose(second.Pose3D);
```
